reasons: Directionally correct: the clause binds our party (Corio, the licensee/customer) to Commerce One's audit, so the rule applies and the edit protects us.

Redline reaches the preferred position with the gaps identified: 'reasonable times and upon reasonable notice' is replaced with normal business hours plus thirty (30) days' prior written notice, an auditor confidentiality undertaking is added, and off-site/no-systems-access language is inserted; the already-compliant annual frequency, independent CPA, and Commerce One cost-bearing subject to the 5% underpayment threshold are left untouched.

Advisory 'minimal edit' failure (ratio 0.766) is not disqualifying here — only one sentence is rewritten and one sentence added; the remaining recitals, cost-allocation and true-up sentences are preserved verbatim.

Comment is accurate on what changed and cites the playbook position; minor gap is that it does not mention the added off-site/no-systems-access wording, which the counterparty is likeliest to push back on.

Caution for drafting review: the inserted cross-reference to 'Section 10 of this Agreement' as the confidentiality section cannot be verified from the supplied text; a generic reference to the Agreement's confidentiality obligations would avoid a wrong cite.
